page: Microsoft Azure E8-2as_v7 is a constrained-core, memory-optimized virtual machine provisioned on Microsoft Hyper-V. Designed for workloads requiring significant memory capacity alongside reduced licensing overhead, the instance pairs an AMD EPYC 9V45 processor with 64.0 GB of RAM. The compute allocation provides 2 vCPUs derived from 1 physical core with 2 threads, operating at up to 4.5 GHz with a 32 MB L3 cache. It lacks dedicated local storage and GPUs, depending entirely on remote block storage options such as Azure Premium Storage.

Benchmark results highlight an asymmetric performance profile driven by its constrained core topology. The AMD EPYC architecture exhibits top-tier single-core performance, achieving 2,860.0 in Geekbench single-core, a stress-ng single-core score of 3,744.98, and high single-threaded throughput in gzip compression and bzip3 decompression. Modern instruction set extensions are well-supported, including AVX-512, VNNI, and cryptographic flags such as AES and SHA-NI.

In contrast, multi-threaded throughput and parallel task execution reflect the physical limits of having only 2 vCPUs. The overall Geekbench multi-core score (3,684.0), PassMark CPU score (5,087.71), and compiling benchmarks fall into the lower quartile. Similarly, high-concurrency workloads like Redis SET operations (3.97 million ops/sec) and static web serving throughput (4.47 GB/sec) register lower-tier results despite solid memory read and write bandwidth in larger 256 MB block transfers.

The primary operational tradeoff of the E8-2as_v7 is its intentional 32:1 memory-to-vCPU ratio. This structure delivers substantial qualitative cost efficiency for database and enterprise software licensed on a per-core basis that simultaneously demands extensive memory space. It is specifically suited for memory-intensive caching systems, relational database management systems with core-based licensing, and memory-heavy batch jobs with limited parallel compute demands.

It provisions 2 dedicated vCPUs from a single physical core paired with 64.0 GB of system memory, yielding an extreme 32 GB per vCPU ratio. The instance includes no local storage or GPUs, relying on remote disks. Benchmark evaluations reveal top-tier single-core processing metrics, such as a 2,860.0 Geekbench single-core score and high single-threaded compression speeds. Conversely, multi-threaded throughput, PassMark CPU ratings, and high-concurrency transactional metrics reflect the 2-vCPU hardware limitation. With support for AVX-512 and advanced vector instruction sets, the E8-2as_v7 is structured specifically for software stacks requiring substantial memory pools under core-restricted licensing models, including in-memory databases and single-thread-reliant enterprise workloads.
